correctness.rationale: For all n≥1, the inradius-one regular 4n-gon has R(θ)=sec d(θ) with normals at multiples of 2α (α=π/(4n)). Its quarter-turn symmetry and Fu–Xie–Li Lemma 2.9 characterize every unit isosceles partner as ±90° rotation. Consequently the full minimization D(X)=inf||x+λy|| equals inf cos d(θ+δ)/[cos d(θ)cos δ], δ=arctan λ. The RESULT.md trigonometric case split m=0, ±1, |m|≥2 supplies lower bound 2cosα/(1+cosα), attained at θ=δ=α/2. Fu–Xie–Li Proposition 2.1 establishes D·DW_S=2, giving DW_S=1+secα. I independently tested all angular regions for N=4,8,12,16,20,28,40,64 and their sharp equality witness; the analytic proof controls all n and continuum of θ,δ.

originality.rationale: Fu–Xie–Li 2023 introduces the invariant and proves the conversion identity and general upper bound, and already explicitly notes that l∞² (a square) attains 1+√2. Therefore the n=1 endpoint is PRIOR COVERED, not separately original. The all-n 4n-gon exact secant interpolation (particularly n≥2) survives; the primary full text examines l_p and affine-hexagon examples but does not supply the regular 4n-gon sequence. Related polygonal James/von-Neumann–Jordan constants are different invariants.
residual_risks: The square n=1 endpoint is known and must not be advertised as novel; novelty pertains to the all-n interpolation n≥2.
Potential equivalent regular polygon D(X) formula under orthogonality aliases remains a residual literature risk; no explicit coverage found.
